common_name: Lapham's Blue Phlox (Unnotched Wild Blue Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring into humus-rich, well-drained soil, including rockier or calcareous sites, in partial shade to dappled sun.

directions: This Midwestern subspecies of wild blue phlox is distinguished from the more familiar eastern subspecies by its petal lobes, which end in a smooth, rounded tip rather than the notched tip typical of ssp. divaricata. Native from the Ohio Valley west to Nebraska and south into Texas and Arkansas, it favors rich open woods, wooded limestone bluffs, and prairie margins, and tolerates somewhat more light and drier soil than the shadier, moister sites preferred by the eastern subspecies. Loose clusters of fragrant, lavender-blue flowers open on slender stems in mid-spring above low mounds of semi-evergreen foliage, drawing early butterflies and long-tongued bees. Once established it spreads gently by rooting stems, making it a good match for naturalized plantings at woodland edges or on lightly shaded slopes where straight ssp. divaricata would struggle with too much sun.
